correctness.rationale: Theorem16 of Cornejo–Esteva–Fariñas del Cerro–Godo–Medina (2026) gives exactly E1–E11 and QE1–QE3; source checker implements every one and the primary PDF page7 confirms them. Proposition21 proves x→y=top iff x≤y, hence upper triangle fixed and n(n−1)/2 lower entries take n−1 possible values. Independent complete re-enumeration (not merely reading a stored log) tested every candidate: counts of candidates (1,1,8,729) and BLAL operations (1,1,4,25) for n=1,2,3,4. The n=3 four tuples are totally ordered. At n=4 explicit valid A=(1,1,1,1,1,2), B=(2,1,1,0,1,2), C=(1,0,1,0,1,2), D=(1,1,1,0,1,1) have min(A,B)=max(C,D)=M=(1,1,1,0,1,2), excluded by E8 at (3,2,0), value1≠top3. Any join C,D or meet A,B would equal this forbidden M. Thus n=4 first nonlattice threshold; no claim for larger n needed.
